Product owner report · revised Phase 1

DuckSuite is a working local video editor. The next gate is a clean render, not the App Store.

A detailed progress summary from the original Phase 1 plan to the current build: what shipped, what changed, the UI/UX now in the app, the append-import loops, the clean-layer review that followed a bad render, and the release blockers still open.

Editor core ready App Store paused by decision AI fill measured limit 83 tests passing 1.0 · build 1 2026-11-11 latest 30d9b8c

2026-11-12 · Loop 7 revision 2 · leftover-text check rebuilt

Review found the check could pass a render that was not clean: hits outside a range were dropped, an early range end erased the line's ink, a line was scored as a whole, and source times were read as output times. One real leak (an emoji, 10 frames at 19.27–19.57 s in the 16:44 render) had been recorded as a false alarm.

Now: each letter has its own strokes and its own frames; a letter is leftover when the output still equals the source there. The fill hole is the strokes, not a box. No fill is reused across something crossing the text.

155 tests · new cold render: 0 leftover in 2,964 frame checks, 40 of 42 lines checked, 2 shown as not checked · hole 84.7M → 55.1M pixel-frames · cold render 698 s (was 418 s) · textfill.VERSION 17.

The render is checked for leftover text from pixels, and two boundary leaks are gone.
  • duckcore/ink.py builds a stroke map for every line from its source frames (edges strong on ≥80 % of the line, weak just outside it) and scores any output frame against it. No OCR.

  • Two real leaks found by eye and OCR at 4.767 s and 93.733 s: the fill plan was anchored to the requested cut while ffmpeg decodes from the next frame. The plan is now aligned to the decoded frame and reaches one frame back from the first ink reading.

What improved for the user

Review is faster and honest: one proof on Preview instead of many, render unlocked immediately, real sizes and paths, and scene rows that match the video.

What improved for the build

Forty-five commits, 117 tests, extracted modules with their own tests, and a clean impeccable detect pass. The app was rebuilt and released locally.

What did not move

The App Store gate is unchanged and was not re-verified on 10 Nov: signing, team, store URLs, review contact, screenshot rights and nested-code signing.

AI fill on moving food: measured, improved, still limited

LaMa reconstructs one frame well when the plate holds still; on the 160 s cooking video the background moves the whole time. A ground-truth benchmark now paints a caption onto text-free frames and scores the fill: the shipped default reaches 23.6 dB PSNR on that project and 23.6 dB on a 4:3 project, up from 22.5 and 22.8 after the hole was tightened. Blur was checked at 90 s and left a visible band where the fill left none. A wider work area, a glyph-tight mask, per-frame runs, zero carry, STTN, MI-GAN and input upscaling each changed the result, none restored real texture. The honest limit: a per-frame model cannot rebuild a plate it has never seen. So fill stays the default, the risk is measured per line and shown before the render, and Blur is one tap away on any line. Replacing the model (not tuning it) is the only real fix.

New licensing gate: NLLB is non-commercial

The optional NLLB-200 600M int8 pack is CC-BY-NC-4.0. A paid $29 App Store build cannot ship it as a bundled or default path without a separate commercial license. Keep it an explicit optional download for non-commercial use, or replace it before submission. The product promise of “no downloaded executable code” still holds: this is model data only.

What this build is

A one-project Mac editor for talking-head footage. Import once, check scenes and speech, clean burned-in text, edit the script, generate or record voice, build a dub with optional music, preview proofs, and render 1080p H.264 offline.

Product promise kept: no DuckSuite account, no upload, no telemetry, no downloaded executable code, one-time $29 purchase.

What changed the release conversation

Two things. A finished 160 s render was reviewed frame by frame: captions were gone, but a 66 ms title at 0 s was never detected and AI fill can smear over moving food. And the store export still fails without a team.

Decision: clean output first. The App Store gate is paused by decision, not passed: signing, store URLs, contact details, screenshot rights and nested-code signing are still open.

The revised product decision

Ship a focused local editor first, and judge it on the render it produces. The editor loop is coherent; the clean layer still invents texture on fast footage, so that limit is measured and shown instead of hidden. Cloud render, subscriptions and the rest of the aspect-ratio tools stay out of v1. The App Store shell must still be fixed before any external build goes out.

UI/UX now in the build

Latest UI captured from the running local core. The demo project is the “Fast 12” fixture; swap to licensed footage before submission.

Toolbar

48 px, traffic-light inset, duck Home, Import (hidden on Welcome), four tabs, Ready, Queue, Settings. Fixed default 1440×900; minimum 1280×800 so it never overflows.

Editor priority

The frame is the hero. Scenes sit left, proofs and transcript centre, one inspector right. The timeline is below the frame, not a second navigation row.

Language of the UI

Warm paper, dark video, amber action, green completion. No admin tables, no model-name pickers, no fake telemetry.

The product flow that ships

One long video in. One local desk. One clean export out.

1 · ImportOne project at a time
Choose MP4, MOV or M4V. With a project open, choose Add scenes or Use full video. The new file is joined into the project master, never into a second project.
2 · CheckScenes first
Scene cuts publish before transcript, text detection and stories. The editor is usable while the rest finishes.
3 · EditProofs and layers
Every scene shows Before and After. Layers are Fill, Blur or Off. The timeline exposes Video, Script, Voice and Music, each with its main tool.
4 · Clean FocusA mode, not a tab
Fill or Blur detected text, inspect every layer, or paint a manual mask. The same clean data feeds proof and render.
5 · ScriptCaptions are the script
Translate English, Vietnamese or Chinese; rewrite for clean, short or punchy copy; reset to source; edit any line. The script feeds captions, voice and dub.
6 · Voice and dubSpeak or generate
Preview a line, generate a local voice, record the microphone, or build a dub. Dub mutes original audio; add optional background music or leave dub alone.
7 · PreviewBefore and after
Review the proof, play inline, re-clean one scene, and keep the same timing the render will use.
8 · RenderLocal 1080p
H.264 MP4 at 24 or 30 fps. Queue, pause, resume, cancel, reveal. No upload, no publish kit, no colour grading.

Engineering that protects the promise

The append work was the highest-risk part of this sprint. It is now explicit, testable, and recoverable.

Append is a job, not a long request

POST /append/job returns 202. The client polls stage, progress, scenes, offset, duration, warning and error. JSON import, upload import and Swift import all use it.

Commit marker + recovery

Check, edit and project source are staged behind a marker. A crash before commit rolls back on the next launch. A committed marker is never rolled back.

Exact timeline

The new video is normalized to the master size, rate and audio shape. Only the new clip is encoded; matching streams join by copy. Offset is measured from the join, not guessed from total duration.

Media auth

The web calls /api/session once. Images and video use the HttpOnly, SameSite cookie. No launch token is built into media URLs.

Busy guards

Check, render and a second import reject while an append is queued, joining, or reading. Active scene reads also count as busy, so Check cannot overwrite the append result.

Safe source handling

Upload copies live only under imports/. Cleanup never touches project sources or history. The last five replaced masters stay in projects/<id>/history/.

POST /api/projects/{id}/append/job 202 { job } GET /api/projects/{id}/append/job/{job} stage, progress, scenes, offset, warning POST /api/projects/{id}/append/upload/job stream file, then 202 { job } GET /api/projects/{id}/append/job active job for reload recovery

$29 paid app: restore is free, no login screen

The purchase belongs to the buyer's Apple ID. The App Store itself restores the download on a new Mac; the app needs no account, no entitlement server and no “Restore” button. There is no StoreKit code in the current build. A free-then-paid model would change that: Apple requires a visible Restore Purchases control for a non-consumable in-app purchase.

Platform floor: macOS 26.0, Apple silicon

Rewrite uses FoundationModels (SDK: macOS 26.0), transcription uses SpeechAnalyzer (@available(anyAppleOS 26, *)), translation uses the Translation framework (macOS 15.0). The app target and LSMinimumSystemVersion are 26.0, so nothing older launches. Lowering it means replacing the speech API and dropping rewrite.

Recommended next move

Fix the output before packaging it. Re-run Check on the review project so the 0 s title is picked up, confirm the clean plan on a 9:16 project at 1440 and 1280, then re-render and compare against the source again. When a render passes that review, the App Store gate can be reopened.

Honest limits

What a product owner must not hide in a launch note.

Editor limits

Trim works. Split, reorder and remove-silence do not. The timeline exposes four tracks but is not a full NLE. Aspect switching is not in v1.

Intelligence limits

Rewrite uses Apple Intelligence first; this Mac falls back to basic filler cleanup. Apple Translation needs language packs installed in macOS. NLLB, Whisper, Kokoro and LaMa are wired; the NLLB pack is CC-BY-NC-4.0 and cannot ship as a paid default.

Audio limits

Generated voice uses Apple say. Recording compiles and has entitlement text, but has not been manually microphone-tested. Dub mutes original audio; music is optional.

Distribution limits

No DMG. Mac App Store only. Archive is unsigned. TestFlight has not run. The screenshots use an internal fixture.

Clean limits

AI fill is a per-frame model. It rebuilds a still plate well and cannot rebuild food that moves under the words. Check measures that motion per line, the app names the risky lines before a render, and Blur is one tap away. A tighter hole bought +1.1 dB; past that, replacing the model is the only real fix. A 66 ms title card at 0 s is now detected, but any text shorter than one OCR sample can still be missed.
